front.title: Generalizing the DAWN MDI for All Entity Types

abstract.t:
The DAWN Minimum Discoverable Information (MDI) information model [I-D.cui-dawn-mdi-model] defines a small, encoding-neutral common header -- three mandatory elements, a short set of recommended and optional elements, and the minimal constraints among them. In parallel, local-discovery work [I-D.jakab-dawn-agent-discovery-mdns] [I-D.blwm-dawn-common-discovery-parameters] has converged on a single-DNS-SD-service-type model in which one generic service type carries instances of every agent protocol, distinguished by a protocol key, with one instance per protocol and a descriptor reference pointing to richer metadata.
This document generalizes the MDI information model so that the same minimal header describes any DAWN entity. In the context of DAWN, entities include, but are not limited to, AI agents and AI resources [I-D.farrel-dawn-terminology]. An AI resource may be an individual named agent or a service such as a catalog that will further the discovery process, and the model is designed to extend cleanly to tools, tasks, data sources, models, workloads, brokers, and application endpoints. The generalization reuses the existing agent MDI without change: the element set, the constraints, and the DNS-SD binding are inherited, and extension is achieved by opening the value space of one element (entity type) and by per-type profiles, not by new core elements. Clients discover agents, MCP servers, LLM API services, and future entity types with a single browse; operators manage one service type.
